Class HistoFitPrep

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.splot.pdata.HistoFitPrep
public final class HistoFitPrep extends Object
Stateless utility class for histogram fit preparation.

This class extracts the peak-finding and fit-vector building logic that was previously embedded in HistoData, keeping HistoData focused on data storage.

Fit-vector layout

All prepare* methods return a FitVectors (or the richer HistoFitPrep.FitWindowData subtype) whose arrays follow this convention:

  • x[i] — bin center (mid-point of bin i)
  • y[i] — bin count as a double
  • w[i] — optional Poisson weight 1/count for count > 0, 1.0 for zero bins (when weights are requested and the bin is included)

Peak-finding strategies

  • findPeakBin(HistoData) — raw maximum (first occurrence on ties)
  • findPeakBin(HistoData, int, int) — raw maximum in a restricted bin range
  • findPeakBinSmoothed(HistoData, int, int, int, boolean) — flat moving-average smoothing
  • findPeakBinTriangularSmoothed(HistoData, int, int, int, boolean) — triangular-kernel smoothing
  • findPeakBinBest(HistoData, int, int, int, boolean) — triangular smoothing plus plateau-handling (preferred general-purpose strategy)
Author:
heddle (original), refactored for extraction

    • findPeakBinSmoothed

      public static int findPeakBinSmoothed(HistoData h, int bin0, int bin1, int radius, boolean ignoreZeroBins)
      Finds the peak bin using a flat moving-average smoothing kernel.

      For each candidate bin i in [bin0, bin1], the score is the average count over [i-radius, i+radius]. The bin with the highest score wins; on a tie the bin with the higher raw count is preferred. Falls back to findPeakBin(HistoData, int, int) if no candidate is found.

      Parameters:
      h - source histogram (non-null)
      bin0 - inclusive start bin for the search (0-based; clamped)
      bin1 - inclusive end bin for the search (0-based; clamped)
      radius - smoothing half-width in bins (>= 0)
      ignoreZeroBins - if true, zero-count bins are skipped as candidates
      Returns:
      peak bin index, or -1 if there are no bins
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if radius < 0

    • findPeakBinTriangularSmoothed

      public static int findPeakBinTriangularSmoothed(HistoData h, int bin0, int bin1, int radius, boolean ignoreZeroBins)
      Finds the peak bin using a triangular (linear-decay) smoothing kernel.

      Bins closer to the candidate bin i contribute more to the score. Weight of bin j is (radius + 1 - |j - i|). On a tie, prefer the bin with the higher raw count; if still tied, prefer the bin closer to the center of the search range.

      Parameters:
      h - source histogram (non-null)
      bin0 - inclusive start bin (0-based; clamped)
      bin1 - inclusive end bin (0-based; clamped)
      radius - smoothing half-width (>= 0)
      ignoreZeroBins - if true, zero-count bins are skipped
      Returns:
      peak bin index, or -1 if there are no bins
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if radius < 0

    • findPeakBinBest

      public static int findPeakBinBest(HistoData h, int bin0, int bin1, int smoothRadius, boolean ignoreZeroBins)
      Finds the best peak using triangular smoothing plus robust plateau handling.

      When multiple adjacent bins share the top smoothed score (a plateau), this method picks the best raw-count bin within that plateau, resolving further ties by proximity to the plateau's own midpoint and then to the search-range midpoint. This strategy is preferred over pure triangular-smoothed search for most fitting use cases.

      Parameters:
      h - source histogram (non-null)
      bin0 - inclusive start bin (0-based; clamped)
      bin1 - inclusive end bin (0-based; clamped)
      smoothRadius - smoothing half-width (>= 0); 0 degenerates to raw-peak-with-plateau
      ignoreZeroBins - if true, zero-count bins are skipped as candidates
      Returns:
      peak bin index, or -1 if there are no bins
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if smoothRadius < 0

    • prepareForFitAroundBestPeakGuarded

      public static HistoFitPrep.FitWindowData prepareForFitAroundBestPeakGuarded(HistoData h, boolean includeZeroBins, int halfWindowBins, int smoothRadius, boolean ignoreZeroBins, boolean poissonWeights, int minPoints)
      Prepares fit vectors around the best peak with edge-safety and minimum-points guarantees.

      The strategy:

      1. Prefer peaks that can support the full requested window without clipping (search in the "inner" sub-range first).
      2. Auto-shrink the half-window if the peak is near an edge.
      3. If the result has fewer than minPoints entries, expand to the maximum available window.
      4. Last resort: if the caller excluded zero bins, retry with zeros included.
      5. If still insufficient, return an empty HistoFitPrep.FitWindowData with metadata preserved.
      Parameters:
      h - source histogram (non-null)
      includeZeroBins - if true, include zero-count bins normally
      halfWindowBins - requested half-window in bins (>= 0)
      smoothRadius - smoothing radius for peak detection (>= 0)
      ignoreZeroBins - if true, zero-count bins are skipped as peak candidates
      poissonWeights - if true, include Poisson weights
      minPoints - minimum number of points required (>= 1)
      Returns:
      HistoFitPrep.FitWindowData including metadata about the selected window
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if halfWindowBins < 0 or minPoints < 1
